title: Worker job dataflow
description: What one worker job does, as a graph: steps (nodes), what flows between them (edges), and which CLI flags or config values change that graph (params). One file per job at worker/jobs/<job>/dataflow.json. The viewer draws it; worker/tools/check_dataflow.py keeps it honest against the job's real CLI.

job.description: The job directory name under worker/jobs/.

summary.description: Two or three sentences: what question the job answers and how.

command.description: How a person starts it, e.g. `worker/worker.sh eval`.

flag_sources.description: Repo-relative files whose CLI flags this file must account for: argparse `add_argument("--x")` in .py, `--x)` case branches in .sh. Every flag found there must appear in params, and every param flag must be found there.

groups.description: Boxes drawn around nodes that repeat together, e.g. 'for each model x case'. A group may sit inside another via parent.

kind.description: input: data read from disk. llm: a model call. tool: something an agent calls. check: a gate or decision. step: deterministic processing. solver: a simulation run. artifact: something written for a person or a later step. human: a person has to act.

label.description: Two to five words; it goes inside the box.

detail.description: What the step does, shown when the node is selected.

path.description: Where its data lives or lands. <run>, <model>, <case> are placeholders.

kind.description: data: output of one step feeds the next. feedback: a loop that sends results back to a model. tool: an agent calls a tool and gets its result back (drawn both ways). control: flow that carries no data, such as a retry or a gate.

when.description: The condition under which this edge is taken.

carries.description: What travels along it. For feedback edges: exactly what the model gets to see.

env.description: A config.sh / environment variable rather than a flag.

source.description: For env params: the file that defines it.

arg.description: Metavariable shown after the flag, e.g. N, RUN_ID, M [M ...].

kind.description: toggle: switches nodes/edges on (they name it in enabled_by). loop-limit: caps a loop (edges name it in limit). selection: picks what the run covers (models, cases). tuning: changes how a step behaves (a timeout, a tolerance, a backend) without changing the graph. mode: runs a different, smaller part of the graph instead of the full run (see runs). info: prints something and exits.

help.description: One sentence, in terms of the diagram.

affects.description: Node ids this param changes, for highlighting. Toggles and loop limits are found from enabled_by / limit and need not repeat them.

implies.description: Flags this one switches on too.

runs.description: mode only: the nodes this mode executes.

switch.description: A toggle flag (`--run-solver`) or an env value (`WORKER_HARNESS=dsh`). A leading `!` means the opposite: on while that flag is off (`!--agent`).

limit.description: What caps a loop: a flag, an env/config value, or a fixed number in the code or prompt.

source.description: Where a fixed value lives, e.g. worker/jobs/oofem/agent.py:MAX_IDLE_TURNS.
